citation: Malek N, Mrowczynska E, Michrowska A, Mazurkiewicz E, Pavlyk I, Mazur AJ. Knockout of ACTB and ACTG1 with CRISPR/Cas9(D10A) Technique Shows that Non-Muscle beta and gamma Actin Are Not Equal in Relation to Human Melanoma Cells' Motility and Focal Adhesion Formation. Int J Mol Sci. 2020;21(8):2746.
description: ACTB CRISPR knockout increased ACTG1 expression and ACTG1 knockout reciprocally increased ACTB expression in human cells. It supports the direction that loss of beta-actin can induce gamma-actin compensation.

citation: Czermak P, Amman F, Jantsch MF, Cimatti L. Organ-wide profiling in mouse reveals high editing levels of Filamin B mRNA in the musculoskeletal system. RNA Biol. 2018;15(7):877-885.
description: This mouse organ survey identified ADAR2 as the enzyme responsible for RNA editing of Filamin B mRNA. It gives a target-specific ADARB1-to-FLNB bridge but tests editing, not neuronal FLNB transcript abundance after acute Adarb1 loss.

citation: Altaf F, Vesely C, Sheikh AM, Munir R, Shah STA, Tariq A. Modulation of ADAR mRNA expression in patients with congenital heart defects. PLoS One. 2019;14(4):e0200968.
description: Adar2-null mouse hearts had strongly reduced FLNB editing but no detectable change in FLNB expression. The result makes the Flnb-editing link relevant but leaves the direction of FLNB mRNA regulation unresolved.

citation: Katoh M. Multi-layered prevention and treatment of chronic inflammation, organ fibrosis and cancer associated with canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling activation. Int J Mol Med. 2018;42(2):713-725.
description: This review summarizes APC as a negative regulator of canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling and lists AXIN2 and NKD1 among representative beta-catenin target genes. It supports an increase in Axin2/Nkd1 after Apc loss.

citation: Ferre CA, Thouard A, Betourne A, Le Dorze AL, Belenguer P, Miquel MC, Peyrin JM, Gonzalez-Dunia D, Szelechowski M. HSPA9/Mortalin mediates axo-protection and modulates mitochondrial dynamics in neurons. Sci Rep. 2021;11:17742.
description: HSPA9/Mortalin knockdown in primary neurons induced mitochondrial fragmentation and axonal damage. It links Hspa9 loss to neuronal mitochondrial stress but not to the exact Shmt2/Chac1/Ddit3 transcriptional module measured here.

citation: Franchino CA, Brughera M, Baderna V, De Ritis D, Rocco A, Seneca S, et al. Sustained OMA1-mediated integrated stress response is beneficial for spastic ataxia type 5. Brain. 2024. doi:10.1093/brain/awad340.
description: Mitochondrial proteotoxicity activated the OMA1-DELE1-HRI integrated stress response and up-regulated ATF4 targets including Chop and Chac1 in SPAX5 fibroblasts and Afg3l2-null mouse cerebellum. It supplies the second, indirect half of the Hspa9-to-integrated-stress bridge.

citation: Xu S, Di Z, He Y, Wang R, Ma Y, Sun R, Li J, Wang T, Shen Y, Fang S, Feng L, Shen Y. Mesencephalic astrocyte-derived neurotrophic factor protects against Abeta toxicity via attenuating Abeta-induced endoplasmic reticulum stress. J Neuroinflammation. 2019;16:35.
description: MANF overexpression or recombinant MANF reduced BiP, ATF6, XBP1s, ATF4, and CHOP after Abeta exposure, while MANF siRNA had the opposite effect. It predicts that Manf loss can increase an ER-stress chaperone response.

citation: Loregger A, Cook ECL, Nelson JK, Moeton M, Sharpe LJ, Engberg S, Karimova M, Lambert G, Brown AJ, Zelcer N. A MARCH6 and IDOL E3 Ubiquitin Ligase Circuit Uncouples Cholesterol Synthesis from Lipoprotein Uptake in Hepatocytes. Mol Cell Biol. 2016;36(2):285-294.
description: MARCH6 loss increased SREBP-regulated cholesterol biosynthesis and lipoprotein-uptake genes in hepatocytes. It directly predicts the observed increase in sterol-program transcripts after Marchf6 perturbation.

citation: Semizarov D, Kroeger P, Fesik S. siRNA-mediated gene silencing: a global genome view. Nucleic Acids Res. 2004;32(13):3836-3845.
description: Rb1 siRNA caused broad expression changes in G1/S transition, DNA replication and repair, and mitosis pathways, consistent with release of E2F activity. It supports increased replication program transcripts after Rb1 loss.

citation: Howe V, Sharpe LJ, Prabhu AV, Brown AJ. New insights into cellular cholesterol acquisition: promoter analysis of human HMGCR and SQLE, two key control enzymes in cholesterol synthesis. Biochim Biophys Acta Mol Cell Biol Lipids. 2017;1862(7):647-657.
description: Promoter mutagenesis, EMSA, and ChIP-PCR mapped functional sterol response elements for SREBP-2 in human HMGCR and SQLE. This documents a direct SREBP-2 input into the sterol biosynthetic genes that decrease after Srebf2 perturbation.
